holes_found.description: CARRY-OVER FROM c2 H1 / c3 H1, STILL OPEN: detail_evidence still asserts that acoustic eigenmodes are 'determined by chamber/sarcophagus geometry and the speed of sound in granite (~5,800–6,000 m/s).' This is dimensionally wrong by an order of magnitude. The 117 Hz resonance is an AIR-cavity eigenmode inside the sarcophagus, not a granite-wall standing-wave mode. Recomputed: v_granite/(2L) for L=2.27m = 1,299.6 Hz and for L=1.98m (interior length) = 1,489.9 Hz — both ~11–13× higher than the 117 Hz observation, falsifying granite as the resonating medium. By contrast, v_air/(2L_ext) = 75.6 Hz and v_air/(2L_int) = 86.6 Hz; the 117 Hz wavelength in air is 2.93 m, comparable to the sarcophagus combined dimensions, consistent with a higher-order mixed-axis air mode. The granite walls supply rigid acoustic boundary conditions; they do NOT set the resonant frequency. A defender who knows undergraduate acoustics can quote our text as evidence that we don't understand which medium is resonating.
holes_found.recommendation: Edit detail_evidence to replace 'the speed of sound in granite (~5,800–6,000 m/s) — standard Helmholtz resonance' with text identifying the resonance as an air-cavity acoustic mode bounded by rigid granite walls. Use the speed of sound in air (~343 m/s) to set the frequency scale, and note explicitly that v_granite would predict resonances 11–13× higher (~1,300–1,490 Hz fundamental for L=2.0–2.3 m), forcing the resonating medium to be the enclosed air.

holes_found.description: ISS-2366 MIS-FRAMES c3 H1. Open issue ISS-2366 (status: assigned-analyst, created 2026-05-31T02:40, source: WIN-003.c3.json) carries the title 'WIN-003: detail_evidence still asserts acoustic eigenmodes from chamber dimensions (c2 H1 carry-over)' and the description 'does not account for the dome author's specific counter that the dome's model predicts resonance from the firmament cavity geometry, not the room.' This is NOT what c3 H1 said. c3 H1 flagged a dimensional physics error: granite-speed-of-sound (5,900 m/s) used where air-speed-of-sound (343 m/s) is required, off by an order of magnitude. The 'firmament cavity vs room' framing in ISS-2366 is a different concern entirely (one that doesn't even appear in c3's holes_found). Consequence: an analyst working ISS-2366 as written will not fix the c3 H1 physics error, because the ISS doesn't describe that error. The decider's routing translated 'use the right speed of sound' into 'address the dome author's firmament-counter-argument' — those have no overlap.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) re-scope ISS-2366: rewrite title and description to capture the actual c3 H1 finding (granite vs air speed-of-sound dimensional error); or (b) close ISS-2366 as not-a-real-finding and file a new ISS targeting the dimensional error explicitly with the recommendation text from hole #1 above. Option (a) is cleaner because ISS-2366 already exists in the queue with assigned-analyst status; rewriting the description preserves the routing decision but corrects the target.

stronger_arguments.description: Numerical coincidence check: 117 Hz / 7.83 Hz = 14.943 → 15th harmonic (0.4% off); 117 Hz / 11.78 Hz = 9.932 → 10th harmonic of Tesla (0.7% off); the 117 Hz value is within 1% of MULTIPLE integer multiples of any low-frequency EM resonance the dome wants to invoke. This generalizes the 15th-harmonic point from c3 H2: any number 100–150 Hz can be re-described as the Nth harmonic of either Schumann (7.83 Hz) or Tesla (11.78 Hz) with N ∈ {9–14, 13–19} respectively. The dome has no a-priori commitment to which base frequency or which harmonic, so post-hoc selection is free.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model is correct that the 117 Hz acoustic measurement (Reid cymatics, ~1996–97, https://www.cymascope.com/cyma_research/archaeoacoustics.html) is a real eigenmode in a real chamber (data/wins.json:003 detail_evidence). Acoustic measurements of ancient stone chambers are a legitimate niche in archaeoacoustics, and the 117 Hz frequency at the sarcophagus is reproducibly documented in the cymascope literature.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Acknowledging the measurement is real does not validate the dome's interpretation. The mechanism is air-cavity acoustics (data/wins.json:003 detail_evidence, where the present text already states 'standard Helmholtz resonance with no electromagnetic component'); the harmonic-of-dome-resonance framing has (i) no specified base frequency that yields 117 Hz from dome geometry, (ii) no mechanism connecting EM dome modes to mechanical stone vibration, and (iii) free post-hoc selection across multiple integer-multiple matches (10×11.78, 15×7.83). The dome takes credit for predicting a pre-existing acoustic measurement; that is the post_hoc problem this WIN already documents.

advocate_mode.best_defense: The c3 advocate-mode defense (piezoelectric coupling in quartz-bearing granite) survives at strength 2 — the granite walls do contain quartz, so a stress→EM pathway is real-but-tiny. But the stronger c4-era defense is methodological: 'Your debunk has built its case on the wrong physics — your own text claims granite sets the resonance, an error any acoustics undergraduate would catch. If your physics analysis is this sloppy at the point you're attacking, why should we trust the rest of your debunk?' This is a tu-quoque that can be deployed against the entire review, not just WIN-003. It survives at strength 4 — the only neutralization is fixing the granite/air error, which is what c4 H1 already recommends.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Fix c4 H1 (granite→air speed-of-sound) as urgent priority. The tu-quoque defense becomes trivial once the dimensional error is corrected; until it's fixed, this single sentence in detail_evidence is a credibility-undermining footnote a defender can quote in any aggregate critique of the review's rigor.
